doc.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

title: Musicians from Central New York
summary: Palmer names many Italian-American musicians from the Rome area and where they went.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well good. You know you come from an area, Central New York, actually a lot of good musicians came out of here.
Oh, yeah. How about the Zitos?
The Zitos, and Montalbanos, and lots of Italians, lots of Italian names.

Rocky Carruccio, Rocky Cole, piano, Charlie French, Art French. Well there were a lot of good musicians out of this area. Tony Johnson, Tony Ginsanti, he went with Horace Hite, and then with Frankie Carle, when Frankie Carle left Horace Heidt, he went with him. And Rocky Carruccio or Rocky Cole was the piano player, went with Patti Page, he stayed with her for years.
